The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. Height 26.2 m |Interred={{ill|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}} (as designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}})
(One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Imperial Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵}} (as designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic Site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |Artifacts=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |Special Notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by Size (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |Map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |Label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large scale complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large scale complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. ( {{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}} ([[Fujiidera, Osaka]]), 5th century) Nakatsuyama Kofun, haisho.jpg|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Nakatsuyama Mausoleum Worship Hall CG Nakatsuyama kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|3DCG (One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Imperial Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵}} (as designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic Site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |Artifacts=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |Special Notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by Size (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |Map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |Label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large scale complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Imperial Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵}} (as designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic Site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |Artifacts=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |Special Notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by Size (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |Map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |Label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large scale complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. rendering, viewed from the northwest CG Nakatsuyama kofun North bw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the east CG Nakatsuyama kofun 5 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front section CG Nakatsuyama [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |Artifacts=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |Special Notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by Size (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |Map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |Label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large scale complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |Artifacts=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |Special Notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by Size (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |Map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |Label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large scale complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Imperial Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵}} (as designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic Site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |Special Notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by Size (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |Map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |Label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large scale complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. Height 26.2 m |Interred={{ill|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}} (as designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}})
(One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Imperial Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵}} (as designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic Site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |Special Notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by Size (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |Map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |Label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large scale complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Imperial Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵}} (as designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic Site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |Special Notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by Size (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |Map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |Label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large scale complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. Height 26.2 m |Interred={{ill|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}} (as designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}})
(One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Imperial Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵}} (as designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic Site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |Special Notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large scale complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. ( {{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}} ([[Fujiidera, Osaka]]), 5th century) Nakatsuyama Kofun, haisho.jpg|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Nakatsuyama Mausoleum Worship Hall CG Nakatsuyama kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest CG Nakatsuyama kofun North bw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the east CG Nakatsuyama kofun 5 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front section CG Nakatsuyama kofun Northwest low angle.jpg|3DCG rendering, side view == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|author=Shiraishi Taichiro|authorlink=Shiraishi Taichiro|chapter=Chapter 2: On the Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. ( {{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}} ([[Fujiidera, Osaka]]), 5th century) Nakatsuyama Kofun, haisho.jpg|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Nakatsuyama Mausoleum Worship Hall CG Nakatsuyama kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest CG Nakatsuyama kofun North bw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the east CG Nakatsuyama kofun 5 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front section CG Nakatsuyama (One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵}} (as designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic Site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |Special Notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵}} (as designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic Site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its shape is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound shape and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |Icon=Keyhole-typed tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its type is keyhole-typed. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, designated as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also designated as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-typed tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Buried Individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, designated as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is designated by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-typed mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-typed mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG.
