The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し|12=draft}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠|12=draft}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|12=draft}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉|12=draft}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun|12=draft}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志|12=draft}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |type=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its type is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, Historic site as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命|12=draft|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also Historic site as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し|12=draft|12=draft}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠|12=draft|12=draft}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|12=draft|12=draft}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉|12=draft|12=draft}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志|12=draft|12=draft}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft|12=draft}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. ( {{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} ([[Fujiidera, Osaka]]), 5th century) Nakatsuyama Kofun, haisho.jpg|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Nakatsuyama Mausoleum Worship Hall CG Nakatsuyama kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest CG Nakatsuyama kofun North bw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the east CG Nakatsuyama kofun 5 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front Height 26.2 m |Interred_individual={{ill|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命|12=draft|12=draft}} (as Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}})
(One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵|12=draft|12=draft}} (as Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |type=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its type is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, Historic site as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命|12=draft|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also Historic site as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し|12=draft|12=draft}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠|12=draft|12=draft}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|12=draft|12=draft}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉|12=draft|12=draft}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志|12=draft|12=draft}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft|12=draft}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. Height 26.2 m |Interred_individual={{ill|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命|12=draft|12=draft}} (as Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}})
(One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵|12=draft|12=draft}} (as Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |type=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its type is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, Historic site as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命|12=draft|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also Historic site as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し|12=draft|12=draft}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠|12=draft|12=draft}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|12=draft|12=draft}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉|12=draft|12=draft}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志|12=draft|12=draft}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft|12=draft}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. ( {{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} ([[Fujiidera, Osaka]]), 5th century) Nakatsuyama Kofun, haisho.jpg|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Nakatsuyama Mausoleum Worship Hall CG Nakatsuyama kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest CG Nakatsuyama kofun North bw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the east CG Nakatsuyama kofun 5 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front section CG Nakatsuyama kofun Northwest low angle.jpg|3DCG rendering, side view == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|author=Shiraishi Taichiro|authorlink=Shiraishi Series|year=2018|isbn=978-4-12-005147-0|ref={{SfnRef|Shiraishi|2018}}}} * {{Cite book|author=Yazawa Kotaro|authorlink=Yazawa Kotaro|title=Mausoleums|publisher=Chūōkōron Shinsha|series=Chūōkōron (One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵|12=draft|12=draft}} (as Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |type=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its type is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, Historic site as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命|12=draft|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also Historic site as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し|12=draft|12=draft}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠|12=draft|12=draft}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|12=draft|12=draft}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉|12=draft|12=draft}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志|12=draft|12=draft}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft|12=draft}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し|12=draft|12=draft}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠|12=draft|12=draft}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|12=draft|12=draft}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉|12=draft|12=draft}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志|12=draft|12=draft}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft|12=draft}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵|12=draft|12=draft}} (as Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |type=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its type is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, Historic site as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命|12=draft|12=draft}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also Historic site as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し|12=draft|12=draft}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠|12=draft|12=draft}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|12=draft|12=draft}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉|12=draft|12=draft}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志|12=draft|12=draft}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft|12=draft}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |type=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its type is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, Historic site as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also Historic site as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. Height 26.2 m |Interred_individual={{ill|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}} (as Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}})
(One theory: Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor) |Mausoleum={{ill|Nakatsuyama Mausoleum|ja|仲津山陵}} (as Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency) |Historic Site=National [[Historic site]] "Perimeter of Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Kofun"
(included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |type=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its type is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, Historic site as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also Historic site as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |type=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its type is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, Historic site as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also Historic site as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|1=Sekkan|qq=}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. ( {{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}} ([[Fujiidera, Osaka]]), 5th century) Nakatsuyama Kofun, haisho.jpg|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Nakatsuyama Mausoleum Worship Hall CG Nakatsuyama kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest CG Nakatsuyama kofun North bw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the east CG Nakatsuyama kofun 5 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front section CG Nakatsuyama {{日本の古墳 |名称=仲ツ山古墳 |画像=[[File:Nakatsuyama-kofun-1.jpg|250px]] |画像キャプション=墳丘（右に前方部、左奥に後円部） |別名=仲津山古墳 |所属=[[古市古墳群]] |所在地=[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]沢田4丁目 |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 34|緯度秒 = 12.24 |経度度 =135|経度分 = 36|経度秒 = 44.60 |ISO = JP-27 |形状=[[前方後円墳]] |築造年代=4世紀末(381‐400年頃[[天野末喜]] 「天皇陵古墳と被葬者を考える」『古代史研究の最前線 天皇陵』 洋泉社、2016年、pp. 60 - 63。もしくは[[5世紀]]前半[https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/soshiki/kyoikuiinkai/bunkazaihogo/koramukodaikaranomemessezi/wanogoozidai/10289.html　巨大古墳の築造年代1(No.162)]　藤井寺市ホームページ) |規模=墳丘長290[[メートル|m]]
高さ26.2m |被葬者=（[[宮内庁]]治定）[[仲姫命]]
(一説)第14代[[仲哀天皇]] |陵墓=[[宮内庁]]治定「仲津山陵」 |史跡=国の[[史跡]]「仲姫命陵古墳周堤」
（「[[古市古墳群]]」に包含） |出土品=[[埴輪]]・[[勾玉]] |特記事項=全国第9位の規模[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html 古墳大きさランキング（日本全国版）]（堺市ホームページ、2018年5月13日更新版）。 |地図=Japan Osaka |アイコン=前方後円墳-南西 |ラベル=仲ツ山古墳 }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|仲ツ山古墳の空中写真（1985年）}}{{Small|{{国土航空写真}}。}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|[[3DCG]]で描画した仲ツ山古墳}}]] '''仲ツ山古墳'''（なかつやまこふん、'''仲津山古墳'''）は、[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]沢田にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。[[古市古墳群]]（[[文化遺産 (世界遺産)|世界文化遺産]]）を構成する古墳の1つ。 実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、[[宮内庁]]により「'''仲津山陵'''（なかつやまのみささぎ）」として第15代[[応神天皇]]皇后の[[仲姫命]]の陵に治定されている。また周堤は国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「古市古墳群」のうち）令和3年3月26日文部科学省告示第48号。。 第14代[[仲哀天皇]]の陵墓であるとする説もある。 == 概要 == [[古市古墳群]]の北部、[[誉田御廟山古墳]]の北東に位置する。全長290[[メートル]]、後円部径170メートル、高さ26.2メートル、前方部幅193メートル、高さ23.3メートルで[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm 藤井寺南小学校ホームページ]、2016年9月17日閲覧、古市古墳群で2番目、全国でも9番目の大きさを誇る{{R|堺市}}。墳丘は三段築成で、[[葺石]]と[[埴輪]]が確認される。くびれ部の両側には[[造り出し]]がある。国府台地の最高所にあるため、周濠は空濠に近い[[湿地]]帯になっている。 主体部については不明であるが、[[石棺]]が存在することや[[勾玉]]が出土したことが伝えられている。また、[[発掘調査]]により、外堤外法面に葺石が施されていることが判明した。出土した埴輪の特徴から、古市古墳群の巨大前方後円墳では、[[津堂城山古墳]]に次いで古く、[[4世紀]]末から[[5世紀]]前半の築造と推定されている。 [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|1948年当時の空中写真}}{{Small|{{国土航空写真}}。}}]] 2021年に周堤が国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「古市古墳群」への追加指定）。 === 被葬者 === 宮内庁が応神天皇陵に指定する誉田御廟山古墳の一世代前の古墳である事から、仲姫命ではなく応神の父である仲哀天皇の陵墓とする説がある。宮内庁が仲哀陵に指定しているのは仲ツ山の南西に位置する[[岡ミサンザイ古墳]]だが、墳丘の形状や埴輪の編年から5世紀末の築造である事が有力視されており、仲哀天皇が在位したとされる年代との間には100年近い隔たりがある。また仲哀陵の指定は[[江戸時代]]末期に行われたものの、同時代の天皇陵の調査を主導した[[蒲生君平]]は『[[山陵志]]』の中でこれを否定し、仲ツ山古墳の方を記紀に記述された長野陵であると論じており、仲津山という名称自体も仲哀天皇の和風諡号であるタラシナカツヒコに由来すると述べている{{Sfn|矢澤|2012|pp=44-47}}。 仲哀天皇はその実在自体を疑う向きがあり、更に[[古事記]]に記述された[[干支]]に従うならばその崩年は西暦362年と、仲ツ山古墳の築造年代(推定380年頃)とは一世代か二世代程度の隔たりがある。しかし、[[白石太一郎]]は実在性に対しては懐疑的ながらも、仲ツ山古墳を[[河内国|河内]]に造営された最初の大王墳と見なしており、仲哀天皇を河内に葬られた最初の大王とする記紀や[[延喜式]]の記述も、何らかの事実をある程度反映したものであると考えている{{Sfn|矢澤|2012|p=109}}{{Sfn|白石|2018|p=98}}。 == ギャラリー == Nakatsuyama Kofun, haisho.jpg|[[仲姫命]]仲津山陵 拝所 CG Nakatsuyama kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|3DCGで描画。北西方向から見る CG Nakatsuyama kofun North bw.jpg|3DCGで描画。東方向から見る CG Nakatsuyama kofun 5 7pbw.jpg|3DCGで描画。前方部正面から見る CG Nakatsuyama kofun Northwest low angle.jpg|3DCGで描画。真横から見る == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * {{Cite book|和書|author=白石太一郎|authorlink=白石太一郎|chapter=第二章 誉田御廟山古墳の被葬者をめぐって|editor=|year=2018|month=11|title=古墳の被葬者を推理する|publisher=[[中央公論新社]]|series=中公叢書|isbn=978-4-12-005147-0|ref={{SfnRef|白石|2018}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|author=矢澤高太郎|authorlink=矢澤高太郎|chapter=|editor=|year=2012|month=11|title=天皇陵|publisher=中央公論新社|series=中公選書|isbn=978-4-12-110011-5|ref={{SfnRef|矢澤|2012}}}} == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Nakatsuyama Kofun}} * [https://www.google.com/maps?ie=UTF8&om=0&z=17&ll=34.570154,135.612413&spn=0.004126,0.007221&t=k google.mapsの衛星画像] * [https://www.wul.waseda.ac.jp/kotenseki/search.php?cndbn=%8ER%97%CB%8Eu 山陵志]、[[早稲田大学]]古典籍総合データベース * [http://www.tamagawa.ac.jp/museum/archive/2002/128_1.html 蒲生君平「山陵志」]、[[玉川大学]]教育博物館 {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:なかつやまこふん}} [[Category:古市古墳群]] [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|1948年当時の空中写真}}{{Small|{{国土航空写真}}。}}]] 2021年に周堤が国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「古市古墳群」への追加指定）。 === 被葬者 === 宮内庁が応神天皇陵に指定する誉田御廟山古墳の一世代前の古墳である事から、仲姫命ではなく応神の父である仲哀天皇の陵墓とする説がある。宮内庁が仲哀陵に指定しているのは仲ツ山の南西に位置する[[岡ミサンザイ古墳]]だが、墳丘の形状や埴輪の編年から5世紀末の築造である事が有力視されており、仲哀天皇が在位したとされる年代との間には100年近い隔たりがある。また仲哀陵の指定は[[江戸時代]]末期に行われたものの、同時代の天皇陵の調査を主導した[[蒲生君平]]は『[[山陵志]]』の中でこれを否定し、仲ツ山古墳の方を記紀に記述された長野陵であると論じており、仲津山という名称自体も仲哀天皇の和風諡号であるタラシナカツヒコに由来すると述べている{{Sfn|矢澤|2012|pp=44-47}}。 仲哀天皇はその実在自体を疑う向きがあり、更に[[古事記]]に記述された[[干支]]に従うならばその崩年は西暦362年と、仲ツ山古墳の築造年代(推定380年頃)とは一世代か二世代程度の隔たりがある。しかし、[[白石太一郎]]は実在性に対しては懐疑的ながらも、仲ツ山古墳を[[河内国|河内]]に造営された最初の大王墳と見なしており、仲哀天皇を河内に葬られた最初の大王とする記紀や[[延喜式]]の記述も、何らかの事実をある程度反映したものであると考えている{{Sfn|矢澤|2012|p=109}}{{Sfn|白石|2018|p=98}}。 (included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |type=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its type is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, Historic site as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also Historic site as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|1=Sekkan|qq=}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し|12=draft}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠|12=draft}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|1=Sekkan|qq=|12=draft}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉|12=draft}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun|12=draft}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志|12=draft}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|12=draft}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. (included within {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft}}) |burial goods=[[Haniwa]] and [[Magatama]] |notes=Ranked 9th largest nationwide{{Cite web|title=Ranking of Kofun by area (Nationwide)|url=https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html|publisher=Sakai City|date=Updated May 13, 2018}} |map=Japan Osaka |type=Keyhole-shaped tumulus - SW |map_dot_label=Nakatsuyama Kofun }} [[File:Nakatsuyama Kofun air.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial view of Nakatsuyama Kofun (1985)}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] [[File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast bw.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Nakatsuyama Kofun visualized in 3D CG}}]] '''{{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|qq=draft}}''' (仲ツ山古墳, '''Nakatsuyama Kofun''') is a [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Fujiidera|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. Its type is keyhole-shaped. It is part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft}}, Historic site as a [[World Heritage Site]]. The identity of the person buried here is unknown, but it has been Historic site by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}} as the mausoleum of {{ill|Nakatsuhime|lt=Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命|qq=draft}}, consort of Emperor Ōjin, the 15th emperor. The perimeter is also Historic site as a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] (part of the Furuichi Kofun Cluster). Some theories suggest it is the tomb of Emperor Chūai, the 14th emperor. It is said that [[Nakatsuhime]] was buried there.{{Cite web|title=Nakatsuhime-no-mikoto-ryo Kofun{{!}}藤井寺市|url=https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/kanko/language/english/furuichimoundedtombgroup/1473315515279.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp|language=ja}} It is 290m long.{{Cite book|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf|title=}}{{rp|98}} and involved large map_size complex social organization and labor. It is surrounded by a deep moat.: 98 == Overview == Nakatsuyama Kofun is located in the northern part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft}}, northeast of the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft}}. Measuring 290 meters in length, the rear circular section has a diameter of 170 meters and a height of 26.2 meters, while the front section is 193 meters wide and 23.3 meters tall.[http://academic3.plala.or.jp/fujinan/fujisi/kohungun/kofun/nakatu.htm Fujii South Elementary School Website], accessed September 17, 2016 It is the second-largest kofun in the cluster and the ninth-largest nationwide{{R|Sakai City}}. The mound is constructed in three tiers, with confirmed features such as {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft}} and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft}}. Both sides of the constriction area have {{ill|Protrusion (kofun)|lt=protrusions|ja|造り出し|qq=draft}}. Due to its location at the highest point of the Kokubu plateau, the surrounding moat is closer to a {{ill|dry moat|ja|空濠|qq=draft}} in a wetland zone. Details about the burial chamber remain unclear, but there are records of the presence of a {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|1=Sekkan|qq=|qq=draft}} and the discovery of {{ill|magatama|ja|勾玉|qq=draft}}. Excavations have revealed that the outer bank's slope was covered with fukiishi. From the haniwa style, it is estimated to be one of the earlier large keyhole-shaped tumuli in the Furuichi Kofun Cluster, constructed in the late 4th to early 5th century. [[File:480220 Nakatsuyama kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Aerial photo from 1948}} {{small|{{National Aerial Photography}}.}}]] In 2021, the perimeter was Historic site a [[National Historic Site of Japan]], as an addition to the Furuichi Kofun Cluster.{{Cite web|title=Notice from Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 48|date=March 26, 2021}} === Interred_individual === Given that this kofun predates the {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft}}, Historic site as the tomb of Emperor Ōjin, some suggest that it may be the tomb of Emperor Chūai, Ōjin’s father. The {{ill|Okamisanzai Kofun|ja|岡ミサンザイ古墳|1=Okamisanzai Kofun|qq=draft}}, southwest of Nakatsuyama, is Historic site by the Imperial Household Agency as Chūai’s tomb, but it is believed to date to the late 5th century based on its mound type and haniwa chronology. This creates a discrepancy of nearly a century between Chūai’s reign and its construction. In the late Edo period, [[:en:Gamō_Kunpei|Gamō Kunpei]] argued in ''{{ill|Sanjin-shi|ja|山陵志|qq=draft}}'' that Nakatsuyama Kofun aligns with the ''Nagano Mausoleum'' described in the chronicles, asserting that the name Nakatsuyama derives from Chūai’s title, Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|pp=44-47}} Although Emperor Chūai’s historical existence is questioned, {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft}} regarded Nakatsuyama Kofun as the first imperial tomb constructed in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|qq=draft}}, supporting the chronicles' accounts of Chūai as the first emperor buried in Kawachi.{{Sfn|Yazawa|2012|p=109}} {{Sfn|Shiraishi|2018|p=98}} == Gallery == File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun 1 7p.jpg|alt=An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the Mid-Kofun period which was drawn in 3DCG.(Nakatsuyama Kofun (Fujiidera, Osaka), 5th century)|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period'''which was drawn in 3DCG. ( {{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|qq=draft}} ([[Fujiidera, Osaka]]), 5th century) Nakatsuyama Kofun, haisho.jpg|Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto Nakatsuyama Mausoleum Worship Hall CG Nakatsuyama kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest CG Nakatsuyama kofun North bw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the east CG Nakatsuyama kofun 5 7pbw.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front section
